newsitem.title: INDIA: Power failure hits Indian capital, two states.
newsitem.headline: Power failure hits Indian capital, two states.

text.p: A large swathe of northern India was deprived of power on Friday after the failure of an electricity grid that supplies the capital and two neighbouring states, officials said.
Dozens of trains ground to a halt across northern India soon after the failure occurred at 6.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported.
Power authorities said the capital New Delhi as well as Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan states were without power. Uttar Pradesh covers a large section of northern India and has 140 million people.
"Delhi, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan are without power," said Jagdish Kapoor, spokesman for the Delhi Electricity Supply Undertaking (DESU), which is run by Delhi civic authorities.
"We have restored power in some areas (of Delhi) and expect the work to be complete before this evening," he said.
The blackout resulted from a major fault in the electricity grid that supplies the three states, Kapoor said.
"It is a failure in the northern grid," he said. "When there is a failure anywhere in the grid, all the states have to suffer." He gave no further details.
PTI quoted Delhi Chief Minister Sahib Singh Verma as saying the failure occurred because Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan had drawn more than their share of power from the grid.
